subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Compliance
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: The ontology satisfies required syntax, language rules, and formal representation constraints of the chosen knowledge representation language.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Complexity
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: Measurable structural properties of the ontology including hierarchy depth, breadth, fan-outness, size, and relation richness.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Internal consistency
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: Absence of contradictions, circularity errors, unsatisfiable classes, and formal incompatibilities within the ontology.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Modularity
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: Organisation of the ontology into separable, coherent parts that can be understood or processed independently.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Conciseness
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: Absence of unnecessary, duplicate, or redundant definitions and axioms; no element is present that could be removed without loss of intended content.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Coverage
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: Presence of the concepts, relations, and constraints required to represent the intended domain.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: External consistency
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: The ontology does not contradict accepted domain knowledge or facts outside the ontology itself.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Accuracy
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: The ontology correctly represents the intended domain when compared with an external reference or gold standard.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Relevancy
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: The ontology supports the intended use requirements for which it was developed.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Functional completeness
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: The ontology answers the competency questions or fulfils the functional tasks it was designed to support.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Comprehensibility
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: Human interpretability of the ontology through labels, definitions, naming conventions, and documentation.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Adaptability and efficiency
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: Possibility of modifying or extending the ontology without breaking existing commitments, and computational feasibility in terms of size, time, or processing.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Credibility
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: Availability of source, authorship, versioning, and derivation information that supports trust in the ontology.

subcategory_suggestion_set.label: Accessibility
subcategory_suggestion_set.description: Possibility of finding, accessing, and resolving the ontology as a published resource.

top_categories.name: Reference-based evaluation
top_categories.description: Methods that evaluate an ontology by comparing it with another ontology, taxonomy, mapping set, or expected reference structure.

direct_cards.title: Graph edit distance from comparison source

top_categories.name: Corpus/data-based evaluation
top_categories.description: Methods that evaluate an ontology by comparing it with source texts, domain documents, extracted terms, or a corpus representing the domain.

top_categories.name: Task/application-based evaluation
top_categories.description: Methods that evaluate an ontology through its ability to support a task, use case, competency questions, requirements, or application behaviour.

direct_cards.title: Scope coverage and out-of-scope term check

top_categories.name: Criteria-based evaluation
top_categories.description: Methods that evaluate an ontology against predefined quality criteria, structural properties, formal conditions, metadata requirements, modelling principles, or quality models.
